hook_text: 600 millimetres up, a pile of loose blocks, and one learner waiting at the bottom. Your team has ten weeks to fix it.
clip_script: A new hall, a raised floor, and a stack of blocks for a step. Most of the class climbs it. One learner in a wheelchair cannot. That is the problem, and it is a rights problem, not a convenience problem. Your team is a building firm bidding to fix it: stairs and a ramp, with drawings, a price and a model. The map is IDMEC. Investigate, weeks 1 to 4: measure the rise in several places, measure the space, ask the users, list the options. Design, weeks 5 and 6: brief, two sketches, choose, draw. Make, weeks 7 and 8: the model. Evaluate against your own checklist. Communicate in week 10: the tender board. Write everything down. If it is not in the file, it did not happen.
visual_style: Whiteboard hall door on a plinth with a block pile; a stick figure in a wheelchair at the bottom; a ten-week timeline filling with the five IDMEC stages; a tape measure across the rise.
pacing: The problem in ten seconds, the role, the five stages on the timeline, the file rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and measure the rise at your own school's hardest door.
